title: EXAMPLE QA Test Case
description: Schema for AI-generated test cases targeting the the target web application. Enforced before every Xray push.

test_case_id.description: Unique identifier following pattern TC-{MODULE}-{4_DIGITS}. Example: TC-INC-0001

title.description: Short, action-oriented test case title. Must be non-empty.

description.description: Full description of what this test case verifies and why it matters.

module.description: The module or feature area this test case belongs to (free-form, e.g. 'Auth', 'Checkout', 'Orders'). QAX is generic — module names are not restricted to any one project.

test_type.description: The category of testing this test case performs. Use 'functional' for negative/edge case tests.

priority.description: Execution priority. Critical = must pass before any release.

preconditions.description: List of conditions that must be true before this test can run.

steps.description: OPTIONAL — Legacy steps array kept for backward compatibility. Replaced by manual_steps + automation_steps.

action.description: Concrete user action to perform. Must start with a verb (click, type, navigate, select, upload, etc.).

expected_result.description: Specific, verifiable outcome after performing the action.

test_data.description: Optional input data required to execute the test. Must be a key-value object, not a string.

confidence_score.description: AI confidence in this test case accuracy. 10=fully explicit code, 1=heavy guessing. See scoring rules in system_prompt.md.

needs_review.description: Set to true if any UI element, field name, or behavior could not be confirmed from the source code.

review_note.description: Required when needs_review=true. Explains exactly what needs human verification and why.

generated_from_file.description: Relative path to the source code file that was analyzed to produce this test case.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this test case was generated. Example: 2025-01-15T10:30:00Z

manual_steps.description: Plain-language steps a human QA tester can follow without any coding knowledge. Must match automation_steps count.

action.description: Human-readable instruction. Example: 'Click the Save button at the bottom of the form'.

expected_result.description: What the human tester should see/observe after the action.

notes.description: Optional tips for the human tester. Example: 'If the button is greyed out, mandatory fields above are not filled'.

automation_steps.description: Playwright-ready steps with selector keys. Use selector_key from example_selectors.json. If unknown, use 'TODO_elementname'.

step_number.description: Sequential step number starting from 1. Must match manual_steps step_number.

selector_key.description: Key referencing a selector in example_selectors.json. Use 'TODO_elementname' if selector is unknown. Never leave empty.

value.description: Text to fill, URL to navigate to, or value to select. Empty string for click/assert actions.

assertion_type.description: Always required. Use 'visible' as default for non-assert steps. Never leave empty.

assertion_value.description: Expected value for the assertion. Example: 'Checklist saved successfully'.

cleanup_steps.description: OPTIONAL — steps run after the case (pass or fail) that undo what it created (e.g. delete the record it added). Same shape as automation_steps; their outcome never changes the verdict.

api_steps.description: OPTIONAL — executable HTTP steps for API testing. When present, the API runner runs these as real HTTP requests and asserts the status code.

path.description: Endpoint path, e.g. /auth/login. May contain {{var}} placeholders.

body.description: Optional JSON request body. May contain {{var}} placeholders.

save.description: Map of variable name to response JSON key to capture, e.g. {"token": "access_token"}.

use_auth.description: Send the saved token as an Authorization: Bearer header.

expect_json.description: Assertions on values INSIDE the response body. Maps a dot-path to its expected value; a trailing .length gives a collection size. Example: {"total": 5, "total_pages": 3, "items.length": 5}.
